metaTitle: OpenHere — Open Finder folders in your terminal or editor
metaDescription: OpenHere adds a toolbar button, context menu and shortcut to Finder that open the current folder or selection in the terminal or editor you choose. Free, open source, native macOS.
heroTitle: Open your workspace, right from Finder.
heroSubtitle: One click, one shortcut. Send any folder or file to your favorite terminal or editor — Terminal, Ghostty, iTerm, VS Code, Cursor, Zed and more.
heroNote: Native Swift app · Apple silicon & Intel
featuresSubtitle: Small, fast and native. It stays out of your way until you need it.

features.title: Toolbar & context menu
features.text: A button in the Finder toolbar opens your default terminal instantly. Right-click any item for the full list.

features.title: Terminals and editors
features.text: Terminal, iTerm, Ghostty, Warp, WezTerm, kitty, Alacritty, VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Xcode, Sublime Text and more.

features.title: Keyboard shortcut
features.text: Press ⇧⌘O in Finder. Make it global or Finder-only, and record any combination you like.

features.title: Copy path, the right way
features.text: POSIX, shell-escaped or relative — spaces, quotes and emoji handled correctly.

features.title: Your apps, your menu
features.text: Choose what appears in the context menu and the toolbar, reorder it, and add any app you want.

features.title: Private and safe
features.text: No analytics, no accounts. Paths are never run through a shell, so odd folder names can’t execute anything.

appsTitle: Works with the tools you already use
appsSubtitle: Anything installed is detected automatically. Add other apps in Settings.
customText: Add any app, with a standard “Open With” or explicit arguments.

steps.title: Select
steps.text: Pick a folder or file in Finder — or just stay in the folder you’re viewing.

steps.title: Open Here
steps.text: Click the toolbar button, use the context menu, or press your shortcut.

steps.title: Work
steps.text: Your terminal or editor opens right there, in that folder.

installSubtitle: Free download. Requires macOS 15 Sequoia or later.
install1Text: Get the latest DMG from GitHub Releases and drag OpenHere to Applications.
install2Text: OpenHere isn’t notarized by Apple. Run this once in Terminal (or right-click the app and choose Open):
install3Text: Follow the welcome guide, turn on the Finder extension, then drag “Open Here” into the Finder toolbar (View › Customize Toolbar…).

trust.title: Open source
trust.text: MIT licensed. Read every line on GitHub.

trust.title: Signed updates
trust.text: Updates are verified with an EdDSA signature before they’re installed.

trust.title: No tracking
trust.text: The only network request is the update check, and you can turn it off.

faq.a: Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account. OpenHere is open source and its updates are signed with its own key instead. You only need to allow it once.
No. There is no analytics or telemetry. The app only contacts GitHub to check for updates, which you can disable in Settings.
OpenHere checks for updates automatically and installs them with one click. You can also use Settings › General › Check Now.

faq.q: The menu doesn’t appear in Finder.
faq.a: Enable the extension in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions › Finder. OpenHere’s onboarding opens that screen for you.
Quit OpenHere, then move it from Applications to the Trash. Disable the extension first if you like.
